title: Forward copy of 12-byte records
summary: Recovered 0x42bb40: forward 12-byte stride, ordered eight-byte then four-byte transfers, per-iteration null destination guard, and advanced destination return. Direct original disassembly and callers 0x429b91/0x43e45f establish custom caller-cleaned ECX/EDX/stack ABI and vector-like bounds; field meaning remains unknown.
test_description: Direct original reference comparison: zero through eight records, self-copy, disjoint buffers, forward and backward overlap offsets 1 through 25 including unaligned addresses. Compare returned pointer and all 256 buffer bytes to verify untouched regions. Empty invalid/null bounds and one null-destination iteration verify skipped reads and numeric destination advance. GCC regparm(3) adapter supplies ECX/EDX with caller-cleaned destination stack argument. Local oracle tests passed at GCC O0 and O2; accepted reference bytes verified against all 47 original bytes. Supplied VS2013 compilation passed at O1, O2, and O2 /Oy- (compilation only).
known_limits: Record field types and original template identity are unresolved; only raw 12-byte layout is established.
Malformed bounds, inaccessible memory, multi-record null destination and address wraparound are outside valid tested storage; original has no validation and may fault or fail to terminate.
No byte-matching claim; portable byte snapshots preserve the original ordered 8+4 copy behavior on ordinary memory, not concurrent or volatile memory semantics.
